summary: Added make install target, honouring PREFIX and DESTDIR , and a native target for a static AVX-enabled build. Changed The build honours CXX , CPPFLAGS , CXXFLAGS , LDFLAGS and LDLIBS from the environment. The default build is dynamically linked and targets baseline x86-64; -static and -mavx -mfma -mavx2 moved behind the STATIC= and NATIVE= switches. OpenMP is switchable with OPENMP=0 , and OPENMP_FLAGS / OPENMP_LIBS can be overridden for toolchains that keep it outside the default search path. --version writes to stdout. SVM scoring standardises the feature matrix in place instead of duplicating it, halving the temporary memory of that step. Reduced the SVM prediction cache from 200 to 50, lowering peak memory without affecting scores. scripts/requirements.txt records the Python version (3.9-3.11) and minimum versions of all dependencies. Fixed Corrected one codon's x-coordinate in the Z-curve feature table ( +1 -> -1 ) in both the C++ table ( include/Common.hpp ) and the Python reference table ( scripts/Zcurve.pyx ). Scores on genomes using that codon change slightly. The helper script directory is consistently named scripts/ ; it had been committed as Scripts/ , which broke builds from the source archive on case-sensitive filesystems.
title: zetong-zhang/clovers: v1.2.1

summary: Web-connected sensing applications continuously generate multivariate time series with evolving behavioral categories, making Time Series Class-Incremental Learning (TSCIL) essential for adapting to new classes without forgetting previously acquired knowledge. However, preserving diverse and evolving class distributions under strict privacy and memory constraints remains a fundamental challenge. Existing approaches often face a trade-off between retaining sufficient historical knowledge for accurate recognition and minimizing the memory required for continual adaptation. To address these limitations, we propose TRACE, a memory-efficient, replay-free framework that preserves class-specific knowledge through generative modeling rather than sample rehearsal. TRACE employs a compact, frozen temporal-spectral representation and lightweight class-specific autoencoders to capture complex intra-class variations. By independently preserving each class model, TRACE avoids recursive generation and catastrophic forgetting, while enabling direct classification through reconstruction-based scoring without retaining historical samples or large statistical matrices. Extensive experiments across five TSCIL benchmarks demonstrate that TRACE achieves competitive classification accuracy while reducing mean retained memory by approximately 98.26% compared with TS-ACL, the strongest evaluated analytical baseline, and achieving an approximately 33.43% relative improvement in accuracy on GrabMyo.
title: TRACE: Memory-Efficient Time Series Class-Incremental Learning via Temporal-Spectral Reconstruction

summary: Latent world models are typically pre-trained offline and kept frozen at test time, so planning with them can degrade under distribution shift. Test-time adaptation (TTA) can mitigate this degradation by updating the model during deployment. Unlike pre-training on fixed data, TTA for planning is closed-loop: the planner uses model rollouts to select actions, and the resulting transitions drive the next update. This raises the question: which objective should guide TTA for planning? Under a prediction-only objective, the model is fit only to the outcomes of its own actions, so it can remain wrong about the actions that would reach the goal, and low prediction error need not translate into better planning. Inspired by reward-biased maximum likelihood from adaptive control, we introduce Optimistic Test-Time Adaptation (OpTTA). Its objective has two terms, the prediction loss on observed transitions and the planner's goal-reaching cost on its candidate rollouts, both minimized over the model parameters. The planning term biases adaptation toward models that are optimistic about reaching the goal, without any additional environment interaction. Across visual and environment shifts on manipulation, reaching and navigation tasks, OpTTA raises final planning success over the frozen model by 13.5 percentage points on average, compared with 6.9 for the prediction-only objective (AdaJEPA), when only the predictor is adapted. When the encoder is adapted as well, the gains are 13.5 and 7.5 points. These experiments span three JEPA world models with different encoders and training objectives and, for temporal straightening, both CEM and gradient-based planners. Our results suggest that test-time adaptation of world models for planning benefits from an optimistic, task-aware term in addition to the prediction loss.
title: Adapt for Planning, Not just Prediction: Optimistic Test-Time World Model Adaptation

summary: We introduce ExCal, a normal-only multivariate time series anomaly detector that combines raw state retrieval, a signal/derivative subspace, and robust statistics across temporal scales. Each expert map receives a high normality floor from the training prefix. During scoring, positive excess is retained, attenuated for broadly firing maps, and combined with a small rank term. The method fits reference memories and projections without gradient optimization or anomaly labels. Prevalence and ranks depend on the complete scored sequence, making inference batch and transductive rather than online. On 180 series from 17 TSB-AD-M families, ExCal obtains AUC-PR $0.421\pm0.37$ and VUS-PR $0.452\pm0.37$ over three seeds, ranking second among 24 methods. Holm-adjusted paired tests detect no significant difference from AxonAD or StreamVAE, which are the two leading non-pretrained methods on TSB-AD-M, on either primary metric, while finding significant positive differences against the other 21 baselines. A separate single-run probe over three series measures median model-wrapper time of $0.0662$ s. Ablations associate the largest primary-metric changes with raw retrieval and excess-magnitude preservation. The evaluated score is decomposable by expert, but its diagnostic utility and online suitability remain untested.
title: ExCal: Optimization-Free Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection via Excess Calibration

summary: Recent studies have applied large language model (LLM) agent systems to computational simulation workflows. Such workflows are long-horizon, so the information generated can exceed what an LLM can reason over at once, its context window. Context management is therefore essential, yet existing systems have either neglected it or treated it as a supporting mechanism rather than a subject of study. This paper presents MarkovSim, an LLM agent harness for long-horizon computational simulation, whose core is a context management scheme built into the workflow. The workflow record is written to a memory system with a predefined schema, and at workflow-defined boundaries, namely the state transitions of a finite-state machine a compact representation of the solution progress is constructed from it as the agent's context. Instantiated on finite element analysis and evaluated on six benchmark problems, MarkovSim passed 16 of 18 runs and corrected its own faults in both the solver operations and the model physics. The engineer was consulted only where engineering judgement was needed. The context remained bounded throughout every run, regardless of its length.
title: MarkovSim: an LLM Agent Harness with Bounded Context for Long-Horizon Computational Simulation

summary: Continual graph learning (CGL) maintains models as graphs evolve without retraining from scratch, while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Existing methods typically target either transductive or inductive settings and often store past subgraphs or require task identifiers at inference. We propose Community-aware Prototype Extraction for Continual Graph Learning (CoPE-CGL), a replay-free framework that uses a parameter-free structural prior, precomputed by multi-hop Laplacian smoothing, to anchor learning, memory, and inference. CoPE-CGL combines topology-infused bottleneck adaptation, community-level prototypes, and dynamic routing by majority vote over node-to-prototype matches. The default protocol assumes each test graph comes from one learned task; a node-level variant handles mixed-task graphs. Each task adds at most a constant amount of storage, with no past graph data retained. At equal storage and without task identifiers, CoPE-CGL matches the strongest replay baseline even when it receives true task identifiers: average performance (AP) is 95.17% and 95.72% versus 94.28% and 95.82% on Arxiv and CoraFull, respectively, with 5.9-14.0 times faster runtime and zero forgetting. Across four transductive and three inductive benchmarks and mixed streams, CoPE-CGL exceeds the second-best of up to eleven baselines by up to 1.41, 6.32, and 9.33 AP percentage points, respectively. It runs 1.3-7.9 times faster end-to-end than the most accurate competitor on each benchmark and scales to the largest benchmark graph. On graphs mixing two tasks, its node-level variant achieves the best AP among CGL methods. The design targets homophilic graphs with community structure.
title: CoPE-CGL: Community-aware Prototype Extraction for Replay-Free Continual Graph Learning

summary: Edge SoCs pack CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs, yet vision--language model (VLM) runtimes keep generation on one engine and leave the others idle. Streaming VLMs expose further parallelism: new frames arrive while earlier queries are still being answered. Engines differ in compute and memory access and contend when they co-run, so no single placement of stages wins across SoCs and workloads. Backend-local KV state keeps other engines from continuing the work. \name coordinates heterogeneous accelerators to execute stateful VLM inference concurrently. It separates a stream's versioned context from each engine's KV state, so any engine can continue the stream by reusing, importing, or reconstructing that state. Stateful Streaming Generation ingests new frames on one engine while another answers, and Concurrent Sequence Generation serves different ready requests in parallel. State-aware dispatch sends each request to the engine expected to finish it first. Each answer reads a fixed, published version of its history and matches its serial reference. \name beats the strongest single-engine baselines on Apple M4 Max, Rockchip RK3588, and Qualcomm QCS6490, even when they reuse context. On two RK3588 video streams, it delivers $19.6\%$ more throughput than the best single engine with context reuse and $27.2\%$ more than parallel engines without shared state. Cross-engine KV import cuts first-token latency by a factor of $4.6$ over prefix recomputation. Stateful Streaming Generation delivers up to $2.48\times$ the throughput of serial execution, and state-aware dispatch cuts query completion time by up to $72.7\%$.
title: Shared Context, Separate Engines: Streaming Vision--Language Inference on Edge SoCs

summary: Federated zeroth-order optimization (FedZOO) reduces the memory and communication costs of collaborative training for edge intelligence by avoiding backpropagation while communicating only random seeds and scalar coefficients. However, existing methods lack efficient mechanisms for exact unlearning to fully remove the influence of training data when users request deletion. A key insight is that total variation stability of the learning algorithm creates overlap between model distributions before and after data deletion, allowing exact unlearning to reuse computation through coupling. Based on this observation, we jointly design two stable zeroth-order learning algorithms and their corresponding exact-unlearning procedures: \textsc{FedZOO-S} obtains stability through client and mini-batch subsampling, enabling \textsc{FedZOUL-S} to perform efficient unlearning by preserving earlier updates and restarting from the first affected step. \textsc{FedZOO-NS} further combines subsampling with Gaussian noise to increase overlap between update distributions; \textsc{FedZOUL-NS} exploits this overlap through rejection--reflection coupling to reuse affected updates when the coupling is accepted. We prove exact unlearning for both algorithms: the model and saved state have the same joint distribution as retraining with the corresponding learner on retained data. We further establish stability and convergence guarantees for the learning algorithms and derive upper bounds on expected unlearning cost. Experiments demonstrate effective unlearning with competitive model utility and up to $56.1\%$ less cumulative unlearning time than re-optimization. Compared with first-order baselines, our methods reduce communication overhead by up to approximately four orders of magnitude.
title: Efficient Exact Unlearning for Federated Zeroth-Order Optimization

summary: Designing building energy systems is a high-dimensional, mixed-integer search problem: when each design is evaluated by a year-long simulation, black-box optimizers typically need hundreds of evaluations. This paper presents AutoEnergyDesign, a framework in which a Large Language Model (LLM) agent reasons over previous simulation results, proposes configuration changes and learns in context from each outcome, while a git-based mechanism automatically reverts unsuccessful changes. The agent couples a reasoning model with an explicit memory organisation (procedural, semantic, episodic and reflective), a constrained action interface and an environment-grounded keep/revert signal. The simulator covers eight technologies (photovoltaics, micro-wind, combined heat and power, solar thermal, gas boilers, batteries, heat pumps and inverters) and computes the 25-year Net Present Cost (NPC), including capital and operating costs and salvage value. On a case study with measured building load profiles, the agent, run with Claude Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 (ten runs of 50 simulations each), is compared with random search, Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) Bayesian optimization and a $(1+1)$ evolution strategy sharing the agent's acceptance rule (300 evaluations, ten seeds). With all three models the agent reaches an NPC of about 3.53 MEUR, 1.20% below the best TPE result and 0.23% below the best evolution-strategy result. It comes within 1% of this design after a median of 18 (Opus) to 27.5 (Haiku) simulations, whereas among the baselines only the evolution strategy does so, in half of its seeds and after a median of 192 evaluations. Opus reaches the best design in all ten runs, Sonnet in six (two runs never come within 1%), and Haiku comes within 1% in every run but reaches it exactly only once. Every decision is recorded in an auditable trace.
title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization

summary: Continuous diffusion language models involve two coupled design choices: how to corrupt continuous token representations and how to invert that corruption at generation time. Recent work has explored language generation on the unit sphere through geodesic and von Mises--Fisher (vMF) paths, raising the question of which forward process to use on this geometry and how much that choice matters relative to inference. We introduce Spherical Brownian Diffusion, using Brownian motion as the canonical isotropic diffusion on the sphere. Its heat semigroup provides a principled forward process, an additive dimension-free noise clock, and an exact ancestral bridge, while a clean-token posterior learned with cross-entropy supports multiple samplers. To separate corruption from inference, we derive high-dimensional approximation rates between Brownian and moment-matched vMF corruption and use this relationship for controlled substitutions. On Sudoku, Brownian and moment-matched vMF give nearly identical results across four samplers and five budgets under otherwise identical settings. In contrast, with the corruption process fixed, sampler choice produces a 25.0-point spread at a sampler budget of 180 calls. Using the ancestral bridge, we split this gain into a memory effect from re-noising the state, present on Sudoku and GSM8K, and a token-selection effect on GSM8K and largest at small budgets. Across reasoning tasks, categorical refinement improves performance, whereas unconditional text generation benefits from stochastic updates that preserve diversity.
title: Spherical Brownian Diffusion for Language Modeling

summary: We present a method for computing a specific type of matrix decomposition that combines a structured framework with data-driven adaptation. This framework allows for an efficient and stable representation of signals or images using frames by identifying sets of vectors that naturally capture the essential features of the given data. The resulting decomposition enables the development of regularization techniques that enhance the quality of reconstruction by preserving important signal characteristics while suppressing noise. We develop an optimization-based algorithm to compute the decomposition and establish convergence properties of the resulting iterates. Numerical experiments on synthetic data and tomographic image reconstruction illustrate the behavior of the proposed method and its performance compared to conventional spectral regularization methods.
title: Computing Data-Aware Diagonal Frame Decompositions

summary: Historical maps contain dense morphological and semantic information about past urban environments, but many digitization workflows focus primarily on extracting geometry, and do not capture cartographic semantics such as building use and construction materials. This study introduces ArchiveLens, a generative spatial knowledge framework that operationalizes historical maps as entity-centric, machine-queryable geospatial databases. The pipeline decouples morphological and semantic reconstruction through three stages: tiled YOLOv11-seg instance segmentation for building footprint extraction; deterministic material classification via hue, saturation, and value (HSV)-based color thresholds; and localized attribute parsing using a quantized vision-language model constrained by domain-specific prompts. Extracted entities are integrated into a hybrid Spatial-Temporal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (ST-RAG) architecture that combines dense semantic retrieval with symbolic spatio-temporal filtering and mandatory provenance grounding. Applied to 445 georeferenced Sanborn map sheets of Chicago (1918-1950), the framework achieves high geometric and semantic accuracy. Beyond performance, ArchiveLens advances GIScience by formalizing historical cartography as structured spatial knowledge representation, allowing researchers to query building attributes and compare spatial patterns across map sheets and years.
title: ArchiveLens: A Generative Spatial Knowledge Framework for Semantic Reconstruction of Historical Maps

summary: Across multiple waves of computing, public trust in new technology has followed the emergence of governance mechanisms that made dominant risks legible and manageable. Generative AI shifts this pattern: these systems synthesize across heterogeneous sources, and users increasingly experience them as reasoning systems. The central question changes from "did it perform correctly?" to "can we trust how it arrived at its conclusion?" This paper introduces Filtered Decision Logs (FDLs), a user-facing transparency mechanism that makes decision formation visible without exposing raw chain-of-thought. FDLs pair each response with (i) a concise decision rationale, (ii) influence-ordered supporting data points derived from tool outputs, and (iii) relevance indicators showing which sources most shaped the conclusion. To operationalize evidence selection, we propose a trace-based method that reconstructs observability telemetry into a provenance tree and ranks evidence using four deterministic semantic and structural signals - Final Answer Similarity, Average Relevancy, Persistence, and Structural Proximity - combined via adaptive weighted scoring. We demonstrate FDLs across three domains: career advising (5 tools), investment analysis (4 tools), and travel planning (4 tools). In a formative evaluation with 50 participants (25 students, 25 working professionals in AI development), 92% rated the influence-ranked evidence as helpful for understanding and trusting the system's recommendation. Counterfactual tool-removal experiments confirm that removing the top-ranked source changes the answer more than removing a low-ranked source, validating that the ranking tracks decision dependence. We conclude that evidence-ranked transparency helps users identify misleading signals and missing context, enabling more confident acceptance, correction, or re-run of system decisions.
title: Visible Reasoning: User-Facing Decision Transparency for Generative AI Systems

summary: What image information remains recoverable from a probabilistic model pretrained through non-contrastive self-supervision without pixel reconstruction? Our experiments show that decoding its frozen representations recovers visual information, although pixel fidelity remains below that of conventional variational autoencoders (VAEs). We subsequently compare fine-tuning a VAE encoder initialized from this self-supervised model with training a separate VAE whose prior is the same model's frozen image-conditioned distribution over latent codes (posterior distillation). Fine-tuning improves pixel fidelity over frozen decoding and conventional VAEs but reduces class separability relative to the frozen self-supervised model. Across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet, posterior distillation improves perceptual similarity, raises peak signal-to-noise ratio by 0.31–0.66 dB, and increases linear classification accuracy over conventional VAEs. Cross-dataset experiments show that the reconstruction benefit extends beyond the pretraining dataset.
title: Can Self-Supervised Probabilistic Representations Improve Image Reconstruction?

summary: When a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model does not fit in GPU memory, batch-1 decoding is dominated by copying expert weights from host memory. Cache-aware routing reduces these copies by biasing the router toward resident experts, but combined with asynchronous prefetching it makes the model's outputs depend on transfer timing, so a harness that does not simulate that timing no longer evaluates the deployed model. We propose prefetch-steered routing (PSR): routing conditions on a deterministic logical cache, into which at most n experts predicted by the next layer's router are inserted per layer and token; physical copies affect only latency. On OLMoE-1B-7B with 50% and 25% of experts resident on an RTX 4090, PSR decodes 2.2-2.3x faster than exact routing with LRU and 25-30% faster than the Cache-Prior operating point, with mean benchmark differences of +0.1 and +0.5 points (95% lower bounds -0.8 and -0.3). In greedy generation its lead over Cache-Prior depends on the workload and reverses on HumanEval at 50% residency. On Moonlight-16B-A3B, PSR is 1.9x faster than exact routing with LRU at 37.5% residency and, at the latency of Cache-Prior, significantly better on three of eight benchmarks. On Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, where copies are cheap relative to computation, PSR keeps its advantage over Cache-Prior on the likelihood benchmarks but not its speed. Distillation-trained gates did not help. Speculative decoding with block-level expert selection was slower than PSR with a 1B autoregressive drafter on OLMoE, but with a block drafter on Qwen3.6 it was 2.1-2.9x faster than any autoregressive configuration with at most its GPU memory on the 64 prompts we timed.
title: Prefetch-Steered Routing: Deterministic Cache-Aware Expert Selection for Offloaded Mixture-of-Experts Decoding

summary: Video world models trained on large-scale robot data promise a safe and scalable approach for learning and evaluating policies that act in the physical world. However, they still struggle with long-horizon rollouts and out-of-distribution generalization, and they remain computationally demanding at inference time. Typically, video world models make predictions in the latent space of a reconstruction-trained autoencoder, which however is not directly optimized for dynamics modeling. On the other hand, world models designed for latent planning usually optimize latents to be predictable, but they forgo accurate prediction of observations in pixel space. In this paper, we show that it is possible to achieve the best of both worlds: a latent geometry optimized to make future prediction as simple as possible without sacrificing accurate prediction of future observations. More precisely, we find that temporal objectives for representation learning, paired with a past-conditioned decoder architecture, lead to consistent improvements in generative video world models at the same training budget. The gains include up to 5x cheaper inference, over 7x faster training, and 15-24% lower pixel and perceptual errors out of distribution and over long horizons. Our world models also agree more closely with real-world policy evaluation when using a vision-language model to judge task success from their pixel-space predictions. Overall, our study indicates that temporal predictability is an important design criterion for the latent space of video world models, and provides concrete guidance on how to incorporate it into the training of autoencoders.
title: Video World Models Need Predictable Latents

summary: Long-sequence models must retain earlier information. Full attention keeps all past tokens but grows expensive, and recurrent-memory models compress history into fixed slots for linear-time processing. Limited capacity makes writes consequential: distractors can interfere with useful content, while skipped evidence cannot be recalled. Existing multi-slot memories write every token to the same number of slots, merging whether to store it with how many slots to update. We introduce Factorized Write Routing (FWR), which first keeps or skips each token and then chooses a fixed or token-adaptive number of slots. Queries still read all slots. Across ten seeds on two synthetic tasks that query facts after long contexts, we observe a density-dependent reversal. With four slots per write, long-context accuracy favors always writing on dense Feature Recall (0.472 vs 0.337), but learned selective writing on sparse-fact Passkey (0.222 vs 0.048). The tested adaptive rule underperforms fixed allocation under the learned gate on both tasks. A diagnostic oracle given fact labels unavailable at deployment reaches 0.372 on Passkey, showing headroom in filtering distractors. The results suggest avoiding missed writes in information-dense contexts and filtering distractors when they dominate.
title: Write What Matters: Disentangling Token Selection from Slot Allocation in Recurrent Memory

summary: On million-node graphs, the memory wall arrives before the compute wall: a GNN that never fits in VRAM cannot deliver the all-node inference its accuracy promises. The standard remedy, pruning, has always been an accuracy tax - paid once and never refunded. DPR refuses this framing. Its central insight is that the mask that shrinks training can also scaffold recovery: one compact node set bounds both computations of graph learning, serving as the encoder's training graph and, at inference, as the anchor from which a sparse structure-aware decoder rebuilds every pruned node (double-layer sparsification). The order is inverted - prune for efficiency, then reconstruct for accuracy - and the tax is repaid: the deployed 30%-budget model trains in 1,450 MiB of peak memory on one 6 GB GPU and recovers 96.9% of its dense-reconstruction reference, beating a same-GPU rerun of the edge-sparsification baseline DSpar by +1.36 pp at 50.1% lower peak training memory; against the same-protocol full-batch no-prune encoder the deployed point pays a measured 2.64 pp accuracy tax for a 2.8x smaller training footprint. Pruning without reconstruction leaves the encoder at 0.378 within the same 40-epoch window (Fig. 4), and all-node serving runs 46x faster than sampling-based GraphSAGE, giving up approx. 5.4 pp of test accuracy. The framework scales to a 2.45M-node production graph at 6,285 MiB of peak training memory; extended variants (long-range context, external text features, a CAN-bus application) are reported as extensions and do not compete with the deployed method, and the 41.8%-budget M4 point, scored on a coarsened super-node graph with its own split, is reported separately rather than compared with the original-node baselines. DPR thus turns aggressive node pruning from an accuracy tax into a safe training accelerator for VRAM-limited all-node inference.
title: Decoupled Prune-and-Reconstruct: Training on a Compact Core with Double-Layer Sparsification

summary: Many mathematical research agents focus on solving problems with fixed statements. However, conjecture research, especially in applied mathematics, may require revising candidate questions or conclusions as investigation proceeds, coupling problem formulation with proof development. We present PACE, a research-proof agent that supports this process through a structured research loop that selects mathematical objectives and develops or challenges candidate mechanisms. The whole prover constructs proofs from these mechanisms, and an independent verifier checks them against the original target. Evidence-tracking memory stores assumptions and dependencies arising during research and marks evidence for revalidation when a candidate or condition changes. This memory supports task-specific context composition that keeps checked premises, exploratory material and unresolved obligations distinct. To evaluate proof construction and conjecture research, we introduce ResearchProofBench, an applied-mathematics benchmark focused on optimization, comprising 51 known-proof tasks with 331 hidden checkpoints under historical abstract access and six open-problem cases. The known-proof tasks assess reconstruction of published results, while the open-problem cases assess mathematical investigation and proof development. On the 51 known-proof tasks, PACE achieves an aggregate Proof Score of 75.16 and completes 20 proofs. In conjecture research, PACE develops conditional results, with its submissions receiving higher review scores than the compared baselines.
title: PACE: Research Proving Agent for Adaptive Conjecture Exploration

summary: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on role-specific prompts and execution models to solve complex tasks collaboratively. However, prompt optimization typically keeps model assignments fixed, leaving differences in role requirements and their associated inference costs outside the search. We present UniMASO, a Unified framework for heterogeneous Multi-Agent System Optimization through the joint adaptation of prompts and model assignments. UniMASO evaluates candidate updates through local, downstream, and global feedback, using cost-aware Pareto search to retain useful quality-cost trade-offs. Topology-aware co-evolution then coordinates these updates according to agent roles and dependencies. Cross-level trajectory memory further supplies historical successes and failures to guide subsequent optimization. Experiments on five benchmarks and five execution topologies show that UniMASO achieves competitive task performance at substantially lower deployment cost than the strongest homogeneous configurations. Under centralized execution, it improves the average score from 69.79 to 70.40 while reducing token-weighted deployment cost by 85.2% relative to DeepSeek-V4-Pro with MASPO. These results support joint prompt-model adaptation as an effective approach to efficient multi-agent collaboration. The code is available at https://github.com/Achilles008/UniMASO_main.
title: Not Every Agent Needs the Strongest Model: Unified Prompt-Model Optimization for Heterogeneous LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems

summary: This study looked at how financial and non-financial support from development finance institutions (DFIs) relates to the perceived growth of social enterprises in Nairobi County, Kenya. DFI support is seen as a way to help enterprises grow. However, there is little direct evidence about which types of support are linked to growth, especially for social enterprises. Kenyan research has examined sector development, social capital, and financing barriers, but few studies have compared lending, capacity building, market access, industrial infrastructure, and policy advocacy in a single local context. The study employed a mixed-methods, cross-sectional design grounded in Market Failure Theory and the Resource-Based View. Eighty-three social enterprise leaders, selected through purposive and snowball sampling, completed questionnaires with both closed- and open-ended questions, representing 92.2% of the target sample. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and multiple regression, with HC3 robust standard errors and a bootstrap check. Thematic analysis was used for qualitative data. Study results revealed that capacity building had the highest average score (M = 4.046), followed by lending (M = 3.916) and policy advocacy (M = 3.851). All five types of support were positively linked to perceived growth (r = .308 to .575). When all five were included in the analysis, only lending was a significant predictor (B = 0.512, p = .015), explaining 45.5% of the variation in perceived growth. Capacity building (B = 0.289, p = .062) and policy advocacy (B = 0.288, p = .145) remained positive but not statistically significant, while market access and industrial infrastructure showed no adjusted association. Qualitative data most often mentioned the need for affordable financing, mentoring, buyer connections, and shared facilities. It is recommended that DFIs focus on lending arrangements that are based on verified enterprise cash flows. Capacity-building programs should be expanded only after being evaluated with clear, measurable results. Efforts in market access, infrastructure, and policy advocacy should be designed to meet the specific needs of enterprises.
title: Contribution Of Development Finance Institutions To The Growth Of Social Enterprises In Nairobi County, Kenya

summary: This study looked at how financial and non-financial support from development finance institutions (DFIs) relates to the perceived growth of social enterprises in Nairobi County, Kenya. DFI support is seen as a way to help enterprises grow. However, there is little direct evidence about which types of support are linked to growth, especially for social enterprises. Kenyan research has examined sector development, social capital, and financing barriers, but few studies have compared lending, capacity building, market access, industrial infrastructure, and policy advocacy in a single local context. The study employed a mixed-methods, cross-sectional design grounded in Market Failure Theory and the Resource-Based View. Eighty-three social enterprise leaders, selected through purposive and snowball sampling, completed questionnaires with both closed- and open-ended questions, representing 92.2% of the target sample. Qualitative data most often mentioned the need for affordable financing, mentoring, buyer connections, and shared facilities. It is recommended that DFIs focus on lending arrangements that are based on verified enterprise cash flows. Capacity-building programs should be expanded only after being evaluated with clear, measurable results. Efforts in market access, infrastructure, and policy advocacy should be designed to meet the specific needs of enterprises.

summary: A circular economy seeks to retain the value of products, materials, and resources within the economy while reducing waste generation and pressure on virgin-resource extraction. In Thanh Hoa Province, this transition is closely associated with the industrial concentration of Nghi Son Economic Zone, municipal solid waste management, agricultural value chains, and tourism. This article uses document analysis, policy analysis, and descriptive synthesis of secondary data published up to 25 October 2026. The findings indicate that Nghi Son offers a setting in which industrial symbiosis can be investigated, although investment scale and nameplate capacity do not demonstrate that material flows are already circular. In 2025, Thanh Hoa generated approximately 920,178.25 tonnes of municipal solid waste; the collection and treatment rate reached 93.68%, while landfilling remained substantial. The article recommends establishing a material-flow baseline, piloting industrial symbiosis, improving source separation, developing secondary-material markets, and adopting resource-efficiency indicators. Because the study relies on secondary data and does not audit material flows at individual firms, the proposed interventions require field validation.
tags: circular economy, Thanh Hoa Province, industrial symbiosis, municipal solid waste, resource efficiency.
title: Directions for Circular Economy Development in Thanh Hoa Province: Potential, Challenges, and Policy Implications

summary: Data, code, and evidence for the article "Beyond Open Weights: Technical, Economic, and Governance Conditions for Sovereign AI in Brazil" (submitted to IEEE Transactions on Technology and Society). The package reproduces the article's three empirical analyses and its figures and supplementary tables. Openness audit (45 large language models). A 13-criterion rubric derived from the Open Source AI Definition 1.0 and the Model Openness Framework; per-model evidence with sources, quotations, and access dates; an explicit inheritance rule for derived models; the coded matrix with OSAID verdicts and MOF-compatible classes; a binding test for use policies; and an independent second coding of a stratified subsample (Cohen's kappa = 0.82 before adjudication), with pre-adjudication matrices of both coders. Cost model. Every input labeled as measured or contracted, with its source (Azure LLM inference traces, NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM throughput, API list prices, Brazilian public contracts, electricity tariffs, Selic rate); scripts for the base case, one-at-a-time sensitivity, and the full factorial analysis over all measured alternatives (2,880 combinations). Procurement screening. Raw results of eight queries to the Brazilian National Public Procurement Portal (PNCP), the screening script with its written rule, and the screening table of 260 contracts with their original object texts in Portuguese. Source integrity. SHA-256 hashes of local copies of all primary sources (copies not redistributed) and commit hashes of the Hugging Face repositories coded. Data were collected on 22-24 October 2026. Working notes and evidence files are in Portuguese; coded data, English justifications, and supplementary tables are in English. See README.md for the contents and the commands that reproduce each result. Licenses. Code (*.py) under the MIT License (LICENSE). Data and documentation under CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-DATA.md). Third-party material keeps its own terms: the Epoch AI "Notable AI models" snapshot and the profile derived from the Azure LLM inference traces are CC BY 4.0; PNCP records are public records of the Brazilian government.
title: Replication package for "Beyond Open Weights: Technical, Economic, and Governance Conditions for Sovereign AI in Brazil"

summary: Reproducible processed-data comparisons accompanying "Training–Test Representation and Reference-Path Sensitivity in a Satellite-Based Maize Gross Primary Production Benchmark". The principal comparison retains 642 site–date observations (489 distinct calendar dates), four maize site-seasons and two regions. A separate retrospective Mead hindcast retains 437 site–date test observations (291 distinct calendar dates); its 480 later-year training observations reuse the principal population. The package retains 120 original B/C model objects, matched cases, dependent nighttime GPP fitting/scoring paths, unchanged validation roles and declared aggregation. The cross-input analysis is a post-review exposed-domain computational diagnosis. It does not establish independent regional or forecasting validation, physical daily-footprint correction, isolated uStar effects or unique causal attribution. The records include the matching Graphical Abstract in compact PNG, vector PDF and larger PNG renditions with its English caption. It illustrates the principal random-forest pipeline and conditional training contrasts, with no new model fit or scientific result. The software includes the deterministic drawing source; font software is excluded and retains its own rights. Neither funder was involved in design, data collection, analysis or interpretation, manuscript preparation or the decision to submit. summary: Raw command log and analysis code supporting the article "Bounding the command emission rate in low-cost robot teleoperation over consumer 4G" (Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics, under review, paper ID 14318).   The log holds 4,485 commands issued to a MyCobot 280 Pi six-axis arm through a browser-based Flask interface over a Celcom 4G link with a Tailscale virtual private network, across 12 sessions from 19 May to 23 June 2026. Each record gives the completion timestamp, control mode, joints, commanded angles and the browser-measured command latency. Six control modes are covered: three continuous coordinate-streaming modes (arm tracking, hand tracking, object detection) and three discrete modes (manual slider, Gemini large language model, voice).   analysis.py reproduces every number in the article from the raw file, including the reconstruction of emission times, the number of commands outstanding at each emission, three service-time estimates, latency by emission-gap band, moving-block bootstrap confidence intervals and a sensitivity analysis of the zero-latency records. README.md documents the columns, the mode codes and the data preparation.   This work was supported by Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM) through Tier 1 Grant H761.

summary: This replication package accompanies the manuscript  “How much coverage is enough? Spatially balanced partial-coverage thermal drone surveys for estimating ungulate density in forested landscapes.” The archive contains the R and Python code, georeferenced full-survey detections, observed partial-survey data, retrospective transect-intersection inputs, survey geometries, terrain inputs, compact simulation outputs and verification results needed to reproduce the drone-survey analyses. It includes workflows for reconstructing the reported full- and partial-coverage density estimates, statistical comparisons, perturbation analyses and post-processing simulation experiments. The original bootstrap analysis used 999 resamples without a recorded random seed. The archived workflow fixes the seed at 42; consequently, some bootstrap confidence limits and downstream test statistics differ slightly through Monte Carlo variation, while the reported conclusions remain unchanged. These differences are documented explicitly in the package. Raw survey videos, MOT annotation archives, raw camera-trap images and event-level camera-trap data are not redistributed. The archive instead contains the derived georeferenced detections and available transect-level inputs used by the reported drone analyses, which are actually required for replicating the results. The camera-trap comparison is represented by the area-level summary values used in the manuscript. Additional exclusions and their justification are documented in  docs/EXCLUSIONS.md . Reproduction instructions, a data dictionary, provenance information, validation results, software-environment details and a file-level checksum manifest are included.

It includes workflows for reconstructing the reported full- and partial-coverage density estimates, statistical comparisons, perturbation analyses and post-processing simulation experiments. The original bootstrap analysis used 999 resamples without a recorded random seed. The archived workflow fixes the seed at 42; consequently, some bootstrap confidence limits and downstream test statistics differ slightly through Monte Carlo variation, while the reported conclusions remain unchanged. These differences are documented explicitly in the package. Raw survey videos, MOT annotation archives, raw camera-trap images and event-level camera-trap data are not redistributed. The archive instead contains the derived georeferenced detections and available transect-level inputs used by the reported drone analyses, which are actually required for replicating the results. The camera-trap comparison is represented by the area-level summary values used in the manuscript. Additional exclusions and their justification are documented in  docs/EXCLUSIONS.md . Reproduction instructions, a data dictionary, provenance information, validation results, software-environment details and a file-level checksum manifest are included.

summary: The geometric characterization of masonry structures with incomplete or degraded surfaces remains a critical challenge in building rehabilitation, structural assessment, and BIM-based documentation. This study presents an automated computational framework for reconstructing the original geometry of partially collapsed masonry walls from Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) data, providing quantitatively defined uncertainty bounds to support informed decision-making in heritage conservation and the built environment. The proposed methodology integrates three complementary analytical components: i) automated wall thickness extraction based on PCA-driven point cloud segmentation combined with robust percentile statistics; ii) wall trajectory reconstruction through the identification of polygonal configurations and structural discontinuities between segments; and iii) slope profile detection using local gradient analysis to characterize wall batter angles. The entire workflow is implemented in Python within Jupyter Notebooks, ensuring transparency, reproducibility, and compliance with FAIR principles. Material characterization, informed by archaeological evidence and geotechnical parameters, enables the estimation of structural height through a limit equilibrium approach. A key contribution of this research is the Best-Fit Model Profile (BFMP) methodology for uncertainty quantification, which derives internal geometric references directly from the point cloud data. This approach allows for a systematic evaluation of preservation states and construction variability without reliance on external ground-truth measurements. Structural height estimation incorporates geotechnical and material parameters, whose influence is assessed through a sensitivity analysis, while the reported height interval propagates the thickness variability . Validation on a prehistoric masonry structure demonstrates the framework’s ability to transform ambiguous survey data into parametric, BIM-ready outputs with explicit uncertainty limits. Compared to traditional CAD-based reconstruction workflows, the proposed approach significantly reduces subjective interpretation while enhancing geometric reliability and analytical transparency
title: Automated geometric reconstruction of degraded prehistoric masonry from TLS data: reproducible workflow and synthetic benchmark (Valencina de la Concepción)

summary: Fix the number $r\ge2$ of erased sampling rows of an unnormalized Fourier matrix of order $M$, and retain $M-\ell$ consecutive frequencies. We allow the complementary bandwidth $\ell\ge r$ to vary. There is a ratio threshold depending only on $r$ below which the two worst erasure classes are exactly the consecutive sets and, after their exclusion, the translates and reflections of $\{0,2,3,\ldots,r\}$. Both minimum squared singular values have the same explicit discrete moment coefficients as in the fixed-codimension problem, now with relative error $O_r((\ell/M)^2)$ uniform in $\ell$. Consequently the classifications hold along every sequence $\ell=o(M)$. A localized polynomial right inverse bounds all moving configurations without a cluster-separation assumption. This forces every competitor into an integer interval independent of $\ell$. A uniform divided-difference expansion then allows the known first two integer extremizers to be used with a common coefficient gap.
title: The first two worst Fourier erasure patterns with growing codimension

summary: Software engineering agents resend their entire trajectory to an LLM at every turn, motivating online trajectory reduction. Prior work shows that randomly deleting 75% of tokens in old turns may preserve agent effectiveness, but it remains unclear why, how agents compensate for missing content, and whether it actually reduces costs. This paper presents an empirical study of 42 trajectory-reduction configurations, focusing on effectiveness, agent behavior, and cost. We systematically explore deleting content from old turns by varying the scope, granularity, amount, and timing of deletion across 9,400 runs with two state-of-the-art agents on SWE-bench Verified. We find deleting large amounts of trajectory content (e.g., up to 100% of reasoning text) can preserve overall effectiveness. Importantly, such deletion must be applied with a delay, as immediate deletion tends to significantly degrade effectiveness. Agents often compensate for deleted content by re-fetching it, increasing both the number of turns taken and the input/output tokens. Whether trajectory reduction reduces costs depends on the pricing model: Under a flat pricing model, estimated costs fall in 26 of 42 evaluations. Surprisingly, under a caching-aware pricing model, zero evaluations yield lower costs, since reducing the trajectory breaks the cached prefix billed at a lower rate. Our findings have three implications: First, token counts alone are misleading; trajectory reduction techniques must consider overall costs under a realistic pricing model. Second, analyzing trajectories is crucial to understand agent behavior, as end-to-end effectiveness hides differences such as excessive re-fetching. Finally, these results highlight the need for future work on memory management to reduce costs without sacrificing effectiveness.
title: The Hidden Costs of Forgetting: A Study of Trajectory Deletion in Software Engineering Agents

Importantly, such deletion must be applied with a delay, as immediate deletion tends to significantly degrade effectiveness. Agents often compensate for deleted content by re-fetching it, increasing both the number of turns taken and the input/output tokens. Whether trajectory reduction reduces costs depends on the pricing model: Under a flat pricing model, estimated costs fall in 26 of 42 evaluations. Surprisingly, under a caching-aware pricing model, zero evaluations yield lower costs, since reducing the trajectory breaks the cached prefix billed at a lower rate. Our findings have three implications: First, token counts alone are misleading; trajectory reduction techniques must consider overall costs under a realistic pricing model. Second, analyzing trajectories is crucial to understand agent behavior, as end-to-end effectiveness hides differences such as excessive re-fetching. Finally, these results highlight the need for future work on memory management to reduce costs without sacrificing effectiveness.

summary: The proliferation of orbital sensing data and the real-time demands of emerging global services are pushing low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks from bent-pipe relays toward intelligent onboard processing. This shift confronts a fundamental tension, where modern artificial intelligence (AI) training paradigms require intensive computation, abundant memory, and stable connectivity, all of which are scarce under the dynamic topologies, intermittent links, and severe size, weight, and power (SWaP) constraints of satellite networks. Addressing this tension demands rethinking AI workflows, from training and inference to the emerging deployment of large language models (LLMs), under a constraint-aware design philosophy. To the best of our knowledge, this paper provides the first survey that jointly covers all three, whereas prior surveys examine these aspects in isolation. We begin by identifying the deployment challenge of satellite intelligence (SI) and deriving design principles for SI. We then examine three advancing paradigms: i) distributed training, where federated learning (FL) and split learning (SL) enable satellite-ground co-training under resource limitations; ii) collaborative inference, which exploits single-satellite, multi-satellite, and satellite-ground architectures to meet real-time service demands; and iii) on-orbit LLM adaptation and serving, which tackles the frontier challenge of deploying LLMs under severe orbital constraints and resource-aware serving. Finally, we identify open challenges and future directions. By bridging the AI and satellite networks, this paper provides a research roadmap for the implementation of space-native AI technologies.
title: Satellite Intelligence: Distributed Training, Collaborative Inference,and LLM Adaptation in LEO Constellation

summary: Replication package for the paper "Risk, not sunshine: financing costs drive the price of reliable solar-plus-storage electricity in the Middle East and North Africa" (Younas Khan and Štefan Bojnec). WHAT THIS IS Code, input data, result tables, figures and a supplementary data workbook for an hourly solar-plus-battery cost comparison of 19 Middle East and North African countries (24 sites: the 19 capitals plus five interior desert sites). The study decomposes the cross-country cost gap into cost of capital, regional equipment price and solar yield, and tests the result against finance shocks, 24 weather years, CMIP6 climate change and Monte Carlo uncertainty. The manuscript itself is not part of this deposit. CONTENTS - code/: all analysis scripts (photovoltaic model, hourly dispatch and design search, climate factors, 24-weather-year test, build-out link, decomposition, bootstrap, Monte Carlo, figures, supplementary tables) and run_all.sh, which reproduces everything in about 6 minutes on one core. - data/inputs/: the input data the scripts read (NASA POWER weather, CMIP6 point extracts, IRENA and SIPRI data, demand and footprint indicators). - results/: result tables (CSV) and results.json, which holds every number quoted in the paper. - outputs/Supplementary_Data.xlsx: a workbook with one sheet for each supplementary table (S1–S26). - outputs/figures/: the figures generated by the code (PNG and PDF). - README.md: step-by-step instructions, a map from each figure and table to its script, and the provenance and terms of each input file. HOW TO REUSE Install the packages in requirements.txt (Python 3.13), then run ./run_all.sh. All random draws use fixed seeds, so a rerun with the default 2,000 Monte Carlo draws reproduces results.json. LICENCE AND THIRD-PARTY DATA The code is released under the MIT licence and the derived results and workbook under CC BY 4.0. Input files from NASA POWER, IRENA, SIPRI, Ember and the Copernicus Climate Data Store keep the terms of their providers and must be cited to the original sources (see README.md). KNOWN LIMITS Costs of capital for Algeria, Libya, Palestine, Syria and Yemen and all hydrogen-chain costs are placeholders; hourly load is assumed, not measured; each country is represented by one reference site. These are documented in Supplementary Tables S20–S22. VERSIONS Version 1.1.0 contains the files listed above. Further datasets will be added as new versions of this record or as separate records linked to it.

summary: SimilCode Benchmark is a curated dataset of 120 short source-code snippets in C# and Java, organised into 60 test-case pairs per language across four ground-truth similarity categories (identical, functional, structural, and different) with fifteen reference groups per language. Every pair was independently classified by two raters blind to the original labels, with near-perfect inter-rater agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.989). All code was authored specifically for this study or drawn from the public domain; no student-submitted code is included. The dataset was used to benchmark four contemporary commercial large language models as similarity analysts — claude-opus-5 , gpt-5.5-2026-04-23 , gemini-3.1-pro-preview and deepseek-v4-pro — with three independent replicates per case–model combination, yielding 1,440 evaluations. The same 120 pairs were also processed with three established classical detectors drawn from three distinct algorithmic families: Moss (winnowing fingerprints), JPlag v6.3.0 (token-string matching) and Dolos v2.9.3 (tree-sitter syntax trees). The record further includes a separate corpus for validating algorithmic-complexity (Big O) estimation: 40 canonical algorithms and 8 adversarial cases designed to defeat surface cues such as misleading identifiers, unreachable code and memoisation. Raw model responses, classical-detector outputs, the standardised prompt with its SHA-256 checksum, the ground-truth tables and the analysis scripts are published together for reproducibility.
title: SimilCode Benchmark: A Dual-Language Source-Code Similarity Dataset for the Evaluation of AI-Based Detectors

summary: This record archives version 0.3.0 of takotsubo_ami_ai_ecg, research software for classifying prepared electrocardiogram (ECG) images as takotsubo syndrome or acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The source archive corresponds to GitHub tag v0.3.0 at commit 341ac955353f535fb74a4b6d8005a8b3b1290ad4. The repository includes retained model-development and evaluation sources, an inference command-line interface, an English Google Colab example, and optional Grad-CAM output for ViT and ConvNeXtV2. It supports ViT, ConvNeXtV2 and MLP-Mixer predictions and their three-model ensemble. Trained model weights are distributed separately as weight release v0.2.0. The default inference input is an already prepared 480 x 480 pixel image. Supported single-frame formats are PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF and WebP; the loader converts images to RGB. Other dimensions are rejected unless the explicit resize option is selected. Resizing alone does not reproduce the study's upstream ECG preparation. Patient ECG images, training datasets and participant records are not included. Paper-default test-time augmentation (TTA) uses 24 views with magnitude 1 for ViT, one unchanged view (no TTA) for ConvNeXtV2, and 32 views with magnitude 3 for MLP-Mixer. View counts include the unchanged image. Raw logits are averaged across each model's views, followed by an equal-weight mean of the three models' raw logits and softmax. Class order is tako, AMI; AMI denotes the acute anterior STEMI comparison group. Defaults include float32 precision, seed 1234, batch size 1 and four workers. TTA results can depend on the execution environment and data-loading configuration. Grad-CAM maps use a separate unaugmented float32 pass for each visualized model. By default, each map targets that model's TTA-logit argmax. These are not attributions of the three-model ensemble or the full TTA average. No MLP-Mixer or ensemble heatmap is provided. Historical reader-study heatmap equivalence has not been established. Validation includes a ten-image float32/no-TTA comparison for the v0.2.1 inference baseline, within the documented numerical tolerance with no class changes. summary: Objectives. Autoimmune hypothyroidism is associated with disturbances in lipid metabolism. This study assessed lipid profiles and cardiovascular risk markers in patients with overt (OH) and subclinical hypothyroidism (SH) compared with healthy controls, and examined lipid changes during levothyroxine treatment. Methods. This observational case–control study included 129 adults: 65 patients with autoimmune hypothyroidism (35 OH, 30 SH) and 64 controls. All patients had complete lipid, TSH, and fT4 measurements at baseline, 8 weeks, and 16 weeks. Lipid indices included LDL cholesterol (LDL-c), HDL cholesterol (HDL-c), non-HDL cholesterol (non-HDL-c), and the total cholesterol/HDL-c ratio. Between-group comparisons and paired longitudinal tests were performed; longitudinal p values were not adjusted for multiple comparisons. Results. Baseline LDL-c was higher in patients than controls (3.96 ± 1.67 vs 3.39 ± 0.76 mmol/L; p = 0.015). Non-HDL-c was higher in OH than SH (5.31 ± 2.19 vs 3.64 ± 0.96 mmol/L), and the total cholesterol/HDL-c ratio was higher in patients than controls (4.16 ± 1.59 vs 3.42 ± 0.75; p = 0.001). At 16 weeks, mean LDL-c decreased from 3.96 ± 1.67 to 3.28 ± 1.00 mmol/L (p = 0.001), and non-HDL-c from 4.54 ± 1.92 to 3.68 ± 1.17 mmol/L (p < 0.001). HDL-c did not improve significantly. At week 16, TSH was within the reference interval in 42 of 65 patients (64.6%). Conclusions. Overt autoimmune hypothyroidism was associated with a more atherogenic lipid profile than SH or euthyroid status. During levothyroxine treatment, LDL-c and non-HDL-c improved, particularly in OH, while HDL-c did not. These observational findings do not establish a causal treatment effect or a reduction in cardiovascular events.
title: LIPID PROFILE AND CARDIOVASCULAR RISK FACTORS IN PATIENTS WITH AUTOIMMUNE HYPOTHYROIDISM

summary: When formal proofs or deductive verifications exceed human cognitive surveyability, does epistemic justification require an agent-accessible chain of reasoning, or must epistemology shift from internalist warrant to structural-systemic reliability? Since the seventeenth-century rationalist and empiricist programs of Descartes and Locke, Western epistemology has rested upon the axiom of epistemic transparency: for an epistemic agent S to possess genuine a priori demonstrative knowledge of a theorem phi, S must be capable of cognitively surveying the inferential chain connecting primitive axioms Gamma to phi. Even when Bolzano, Frege, and Russell purged psychologism and spatio-temporal intuition from deductive logic, they treated formalization as a vehicle for rendering every inferential transition perspicuous to rational inspection. However, automated theorem provers, Boolean satisfiability (SAT) solvers, and interactive proof assistants routinely generate formal derivations that are deductively sound yet impossible for any finite biological mind to survey in full—violating the Wittgensteinian criterion of cognitive surveyability (Übersichtlichkeit). This paper provides a systematic formal and historical analysis of this problem across eight sections: (1) Section 1 reconstructs the classical transparency paradigm across Descartes, Leibniz, Locke, and Kant, isolating the working-memory and temporal synthesis bounds built into classical deductio; (2) Section 2 demonstrates how the Bolzanian-Fregean-Hilbertian quest for local step-wise gaplessness (Lückenlosigkeit) triggered an inverse scaling law that dialectically destroyed global proof surveyability; (3) Section 3 analyzes the Wittgensteinian critique of un-surveyable derivations, formalizing the distinction between a normative grammatical criterion and an empirical physical experiment; (4) Section 4 proves via Gödelian speed-up, Gentzen cut-elimination, and propositional proof complexity lower bounds that trans-surveyable derivations (||D|| >> kappa(S)) are an inescapable metamathematical feature of formal systems rather than an artifact of unoptimized proof search; (5) Section 5 introduces Bounded Justification Logic (BJL_kappa), formally deriving the inconsistency of the Classical Surveyability Trilemma; (6) Section 6 evaluates the Tymoczko–Burge–Kripke debate on computer-assisted proofs, refuting both quasi-empiricist hardware inductivism and ungrounded testimonial transmission; (7) Section 7 constructs a positive theory of Structural-Systemic Warrant (SSW), demonstrating how de Bruijn meta-kernel soundness compression and substrate-invariant equivalence preserve derivative a priori warrant while bifurcating demonstrative warrant (Dass-Wissen) from explanatory illumination (Warum-Wissen); (8) Section 8 addresses foundational objections from rule-following skepticism, Gödelian second-incompleteness limits, and zero-knowledge probabilistic verification (ZKPs and PCPs), synthesizing the general epistemological conclusions.
title: Epistemic Justification Beyond Cognitive Surveyability: A Formal and Historical Account of Deductive Warrant under Trans-Cognitive Verification

summary: The book as a PDF, in the shape it is printed: read it in the browser at https://h0ffmann.github.io/closed-source/paper.pdf , or download it from the newest release at https://github.com/h0ffmann/closed-source/releases/latest/download/closed-source.pdf . The files of this record are the source that builds that PDF. A position paper arguing that closed source has failed as a protection, for science first. It reads the case through Robert M. Pirsig's Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance (1974), the book it stands on: the number of rational hypotheses that can explain a phenomenon is infinite, so science never closes, and a method that only its owner can open is one that nobody else can test. Large language models now decompile binaries into re-executable source; black-box queries extract parts of production models; distillation copies capabilities at industrial scale; and the largest 2026 trade-secret dispute in artificial intelligence, Apple's suit against OpenAI, turns on people, laptops and recruiting rather than on code that stayed secret. Against this background the paper revisits Linus Torvalds' Linux and Git as evidence that openness scales, and the author's closed undergraduate thesis as evidence of what secrecy costs a researcher. It argues that the ethical answer to universal reverse engineering is professional citation, proposes three rules for AI agents (borrow, cite, propagate), and describes Paper Fabric, the open pipeline in the Ouroboric style that produced it. This record is a book. It has not been peer reviewed. It holds the source of the book at the release tag: the Markdown text, the build and the agent configuration. The rendered PDFs are attached to the GitHub release of the same tag. The writer develops in the open. His three other works each have a permanent DOI, and this record cites all three: marola, an open, non-profit platform for sea conditions and bathing-water quality, written with five other people ( 10.5281/zenodo.23224155 ); WW3 GPU Lab, a bit-for-bit GPU port of WAVEWATCH III ( 10.5281/zenodo.23221351 ); and picasso, Nix flakes for scientific and agentic toolchains, which builds this book ( 10.5281/zenodo.23311208 ). The book is made in the Ouroboric style, and the Ouroboric ideas are Bruno Valério's ( https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/ouroboric ); Ouroboric has no DOI yet, so this record cites it by its address.
title: Closed Source: The God that Failed

summary: A staged, reproducible pipeline for VLT/MUSE narrow-field-mode integral-field data: raw-cube reduction, spectral extraction of a faint companion next to a much brighter primary star with six independent extraction schemes, and hydrogen-line accretion analysis with detection limits calibrated against empirical nulls from control positions processed identically to the object. Every stage emits a machine-readable quality-control document, and later stages read those documents rather than trusting assumptions; provenance (input cube, SHA-256 hashes, specification version, wavelength frame, flux unit) travels with the products. Research code under active development. This is the version used in Ramírez Reyes & Cáceres (in preparation).
title: MUSE accretion pipeline

summary: EXTERNAL QIGONG AND HUMAN THERMAL RADIATION PATTERNS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English research working monograph investigating whether thermographic differences observed during culturally defined qigong and matched neutral tasks can be distinguished from ordinary human thermoregulation, environmental exchange and measurement bias. The governing three-coupling is infrared thermal imaging x physiological regulation x heat-transfer models. The research treats “external qi” as a cultural and experimental task label, not an established physical energy carrier. The scientific core separates raw infrared radiance from inferred skin temperature and estimated heat flux. It develops emissivity and reflected-wall correction, blackbody calibration, spectral detector response, conduction and perfusion bioheat models, convection, evaporation, respiration-related temperature patterns, posture and muscular activity. The original candidate bulk heat equation is explicitly refined by separating volumetric tissue transport from surface heat-transfer boundary conditions. The principal proposed test uses concealed task assignments, matched breathing/movement/clothing, phantom references, negative-control regions and conventional physics-first rivals. Thirty physically distinct mathematical plates document governing relationships, units, assumptions, identifiability, masked falsifiers and chapter links. Eighty-two independent research chapters contain 410 single-page investigations. The true center of the monograph is its 200 one-page Research Gates, each posing a falsifiable question in bold deep-navy typography and asking what an independent successor must measure, challenge, disprove or preserve. Thirty-three differentiated Phoenix Answer Embryos propose future instruments, error-correction artifacts, negative-result protocols and reproducibility tools. The DOI registry separates three STARLI author mother volumes from eleven externally published methodological or conventional-science references on infrared thermography, emissivity, classical bioheat and research design. Bibliographic sources constrain methods; they do not validate extraordinary qigong mechanisms. Every integrated experiment is prospective. The book presents no completed human intervention, clinically established effect, new physical particle or evidence of treatment efficacy. Ethical authorization and independent scientific review would be required before future human-observation research. Author: 33 | STARLI White Rainbow Epoch Series: STARLI Research Institute XXXIII | Flagship 38 of 90

summary: Human observers can encounter representations of the same relational contribution history yet form different beliefs about its significance and trustworthiness. This third paper in a coordinated research programme investigates cognitive processes between the structural availability of evidence and an observer’s assessment of a person, claim, or contribution. Its proposed analytic objects are selective attention, evidence encoding, reconstructive memory, attribution, interpretive schemas, belief revision, epistemic vigilance, and behavioral reliance. The inquiry distinguishes evidentiary accessibility from cognitive encounter, subjective confidence from justified assessment, and expressed trust from risk-bearing cooperation. Prior work in attention, working memory, judgment under uncertainty, epistemic vigilance, and trust in automation motivates a provisional sequential-kernel architecture; that architecture remains a research proposal rather than a validated general cognitive model. AI-mediated information environments supply a historically relevant application, without defining the paper’s full scope. This working draft contains all ten planned sections, covering cognitive interfaces, selective attention, memory-based trajectory reconstruction, contribution attribution, proposition-specific belief revision, testimony evaluation, behavioral reliance, empirical designs with explicit identification boundaries, and a synthesis of conditional theoretical findings. It reports no original empirical results.
title: Cognitive Mediation of Relational Evidence: An Investigation of Epistemic Judgment and Reliance

summary: Aviation authorities hold decades of accident reports whose narratives record how investigators reconstructed each accident. Computational work on these archives has mostly sorted reports into fixed taxonomies. In this work, we propose a hybrid framework in which a text-based corpus identifies the leading factors of a failure mode. Physics-based models then quantify how likely that failure is at a stated operating point. Ordered causal chains extracted from 56,202 American accident reports with a local large language model aggregate into a causation knowledge graph. On an evaluation sample of 2,000 reports, the chains recover 90.8% of investigator-flagged causes. Each physical factor whose drivers the record carries receives an occurrence model calibrated to the accident population. A leaky noisy-OR fitted to the corpus combines the factors into a failure mode probability that supports intervention. For engine power loss, the carburetor icing model separates 1,205 icing accidents from other accidents using temperature and dewpoint alone, reaching 0.61 in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve against a density ratio ceiling of 0.64. Routine weather hours give no valid control, because flying concentrates in fair weather. On later years the physics adds 0.03 to that area for occurrence and nothing for severity, so its value lies in interpretability. On four named accidents, abduction gives a probability of necessity of 0.29 to 0.50 for the heat omission, under monotonicity. The Fast Causal Inference algorithm does not license the largest backdoor adjustment on the learned networks.
title: A Hybrid Framework for Explainable Aviation Risk: Causal Chain Extraction from Safety Reports with Physics-Based Failure Quantification and Interventional Analysis

summary: Software development with coding agents often begins with a rough request that users refine after trying the implementation. Final correctness alone does not capture the repeated guidance this process requires. We introduce FeatureLoop, a benchmark of 61 human-reviewed tasks from 34 repositories across five primary programming languages and seven software forms. Each task follows one development goal in a persistent workspace through evolution feedback, which adds or clarifies requirements, and completion feedback, which reports failures of stated requirements. Cumulative executable checks track new behavior, repair, and preservation of earlier functionality. We evaluate 12 frontier models and find that the strongest completes 72.1% of tasks with both feedback types. Across models, however, only 15.4% of observed failed stages recover within two corrective revisions. Further analysis reveals incomplete repairs, regressions, and model-specific differences in feedback use and token efficiency, identifying obstacles to reliable, low-intervention development.
title: FeatureLoop: Benchmarking Coding Agents under Evolving Requirements

summary: Machine learning models are now widely used to predict environmental variable dynamics in domains like hydrology, climate science, agriculture, and ecology. These models are usually compared on fixed benchmark datasets using a single average accuracy score. As models improve, their scores become very close when averaged over large regions and long time periods, so the benchmark can no longer tell them apart, and a single number hides \emph{where} and \emph{when} a model fails. Three failures are common across environmental domains: models get worse as the climate shifts (non-stationarity), models fail at unmonitored sites (spatial extrapolation), and models miss rare but important regimes such as floods and droughts. We present \textbf{EvoBench}, a benchmark framework that shows where a model fails, tracks failures over time, and evolves to focus on model capability gaps. We apply EvoBench to daily streamflow prediction as a case study (\textbf{CAMELS-Evolve}, about 9{,}000 U.S. basins, 1985--2024) and compare an operational physical model (NWM), a conceptual reference (HBV), and several data-driven models. No model wins on every testing scenarios (e.g., in terms of average accuracy, performance at low flows and unmonitored basins). Also we observe that all data-driven models under-predict floods. Additionally, we show that targeted fix based on the reported failures could mitigate weaknesses the benchmark identified in certain scenarios. EvoBench turns model evaluation from a saturated ranking into a moving map of model limitations.
title: EvoBench: An Evolving, Diagnostic Benchmark Framework for Environmental Modeling

summary: AI-powered personal assistant frameworks such as OpenClaw combine LLM reasoning, persistent memory, tool invocation, local execution, and web-based workflows. These capabilities enable useful automation, but they also create security risks when untrusted inputs, model reasoning, tools, memory, and deployment configuration interact without explicit trust boundaries. This paper presents an empirical study of reported security concerns in OpenClaw using two complementary data sources: Reddit discussions and security-tagged GitHub issues. We analyze more than 25K Reddit posts from 13 OpenClaw-related subreddits and identify 162 security-relevant posts with 1,787 associated comments. We further collect 358 security-tagged GitHub issues and retain 180 issues describing concrete security concerns. Using qualitative analysis and evidence-grounded CWE mapping, we identify 521 CWE instances across 59 distinct weakness types, concentrated in access-control failures, sensitive-data exposure, injection, and unsafe execution. We also extract 543 practitioner mitigation suggestions and consolidate them into seven recurring strategies. To complement the empirical analysis, we present an evidence-grounded illustrative reconstruction of a representative sensitive-data exposure pathway using dummy secret values. Our findings show that OpenClaw security issues are not isolated implementation bugs; they reflect recurring trust-boundary failures across the agent execution pipeline. We discuss how these weaknesses map to both traditional software-security categories and agent-specific failure mechanisms, and derive implications for safer agentic systems, including explicit trust boundaries, least-privilege tool access, execution containment, runtime oversight, and defense-in-depth deployment.
title: Then there is prompt injection, a malicious email, ...: The Wild Wide West of OpenClaw Agentic System Security
